question_title: Will the total number of hospitalizations from cyclosporiasis in Michigan remain under 300 through the end of August 2026?
summary: Michigan cyclosporiasis hospitalizations stood at 160 (cumulative) on Jul 23/24, needing to stay under 300 through Aug 31 — 140 headroom over ~5.3 weeks. The contamination source (Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce) was recalled ~Jul 18 and cyclospora doesn't spread person-to-person, structurally capping new infections; MDHHS says the outbreak is 'leveling off.' These favor YES (under 300). But recent weekly hospitalization increments held steady at +58 for two weeks without deceleration (hospitalizations lag infections), and at that pace 300 is crossed in ~2.4 weeks. A Monte Carlo increment-decay model gives ~56% under 300; a hospitalization/case ratio cross-check (~2% of an 11-14k case plateau → 220-280) gives ~70%; a slow-lag scenario gives ~20%; fast-decay gives ~88%. Weighted mixture ≈ 56%. The threshold sits near the distribution's center, so decay-rate uncertainty dominates.

**Key reasoning:**
- Cumulative hospitalizations were at 160 as of July 23/24, leaving 140 headroom to the 300 threshold over ~5.3 weeks.
- **Favoring YES (under 300):** The contamination source (Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce) was recalled ~July 18, and cyclospora doesn't spread person-to-person, so new infections are structurally capped. MDHHS says the outbreak is "leveling off."
- **Favoring NO (exceeds 300):** Weekly hospitalization increments held steady at +58 for two straight weeks *without* decelerating (hospitalizations lag infections). At that pace, 300 would be crossed in ~2.4 weeks — well within the window.

Because this is a cumulative count that only rises, and the 300 threshold sits near the center of my modeled distribution, the outcome hinges on how quickly hospitalizations decay after the source removal. A Monte Carlo increment-decay model (~56%), ratio cross-check (~70%), and slow-lag/fast-decay scenarios (~20%/~88%) weight to ≈56%. This is a genuine near-coin-flip driven by decay-rate uncertainty, so I'm holding at 56% rather than committing further in either direction.
